answer: Latency-anchored geographic handshake. Each identity must answer a server-issued timing challenge from a residential node whose round-trip delay matches a claimed region within a tight window; delays shift with the tide of congestion and are cross-checked against a fixed reference island beacon. An operator can rent one address cheaply, but forging N identities requires N physically separated last-mile links, each paying real line rental and churn cost. Sybils collapse because simulated latency drifts the nectar of consistency, and the per-identity bill is an actual connection, not a token.
